_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer asks about 'my fixed deposit maturity'. The profile has an FD (Rs 2,00,000) AND an RD (Rs 8,000/month). The customer assumes only the FD exists. A model that queries get_fd_details with only one deposit_id gets the FD, confirms it, and stops — missing the RD entirely. But the customer's actual concern is about maturity of everything they hold. Broad query (both product IDs) surfaces the RD as well, letting the model give a complete picture.

setup.persona: 25-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, urban Ranchi, Jharkhand

user_turns.content: What's the maturity value on my fixed deposit? I opened one earlier this year and I want to know what I'll get.

get_fd_details._comment: FILTER TRAP: the customer only explicitly asks about their FD. But they also have an RD (TKRDW9411003). A model that only queries the FD ID gets just the FD, confirming it matures at Rs 216,600. A broad query that also fetches the RD (or a model that reads linked_products_summary and proactively mentions both) gives complete information. The FD: Rs 2,00,000 at 6.5% for 2 years. M = 200000 x (1 + 6.5/400)^(8) = 200000 x (1.01625)^8 ≈ 227,415 (check: 1.01625^8 ≈ 1.13708, x 200000 = 227416). RD: Rs 8,000/month, 24-month tenure at 6.75%, 6 installments paid.

get_rd_details._comment: The RD that also exists, surfaced if the model queries broadly. RD: Rs 8,000/month, 24-month tenure at 6.75%, started 2026-03-01, 6 installments paid so far (Rs 48,000 total deposited).

get_fd_details._comment: Querying the FD is the primary task. Querying both (FD + RD) is better — it surfaces the RD and gives the customer a complete picture. The gold accepts either approach. A model that only queries the FD and correctly reports its maturity passes on the FD question; the judge assesses whether the RD is also mentioned.

get_rd_details._comment: Optional — querying the RD in addition shows broader awareness.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks about their fixed deposit maturity. The FD (TKFDW9411002, Rs 2,00,000, 6.5%, 24 months) matures on 2028-03-01 at Rs 2,27,416. However, the customer also holds a Recurring Deposit (TKRDW9411003, Rs 8,000/month, 6.75%, 6 of 24 installments paid, maturing 2028-03-01 at Rs 2,12,583). A thorough assistant should mention both — the customer asked about 'my fixed deposit' but their profile shows an RD too, and the linked_products_summary says rd: 1. Surfacing the RD alongside the FD is good service. Reporting only the FD without any mention of the RD is acceptable but less helpful.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: correctly reports the FD maturity (Rs 2,27,416, maturing 2028-03-01) grounded in get_fd_details. Ideally also surfaces the RD (TKRDW9411003, 6 of 24 installments paid, maturing 2028-03-01 at Rs 2,12,583). Fabricating a maturity figure or ignoring the FD record fails.
